archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing-and-accuracy)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower in Liam Coen's structure who wins from the pocket at 10-19 yards and over the middle, with his legs now an afterthought rather than a second engine.

report.headline: Same depth, far better accuracy: Lawrence's leap is partly real, partly a hot month.
report.take:
Lawrence has spent five seasons as a high-volume, mistake-prone passer with useful legs. He finished outside the top 40 in CPOE in three of the last four years and ranked 60th or worse in interceptions three times. Four games into 2026 he leads all 42 qualifiers at +10.4 CPOE and sits ninth in EPA per dropback at 0.283. The interesting part is that he hasn't bought that accuracy by throwing shorter. His intended air yards (9.07) match last year's 9.0 aDOT, and his bad-throw rate has dropped to 7.7%, eighth-best, after sitting between 13.9% and 19.8% for his whole career. He's throwing to the same spots and missing far less often.

The engine is the intermediate game and the middle of the field. On 35 throws of 10-19 air yards he's at +0.62 EPA with a 68.6% success rate, and his 18 middle-of-field throws produce +0.87 EPA and four touchdowns. The offense also clearly prefers him in shotgun: +0.35 EPA there against +0.09 under center. Jakobi Meyers (+1.22 EPA per target on 15 looks) has been the big-play outlet, while Parker Washington soaks up the volume with 26 targets.

The numbers flatter him in a few places. A 7.7% touchdown rate, sixth in the league, is well above anything in his career; even his 29-TD 2025 ran closer to 5%. Six red-zone scores on 17 attempts at 52.9% completion will cool off. The deep EPA (+0.94) comes on 10 attempts with four completions, which is a few plays, not a trait. He's also taken eight sacks on just 16.7% pressure, because 22% of pressures become sacks, and the line ranks 29th in hit rate allowed. His rushing has nearly vanished: 34 yards and two scrambles after four straight seasons near 300+ yards outside the injured 2024. Close fourth quarters (13 plays, -9.2 CPOE) are a tiny sample but not a reassuring one.

Where this goes: the accuracy gain probably holds in part, since the bad-throw drop is broad-based and not one hot game. Expect CPOE to settle in the positive single digits and the TD rate to fall back toward 5%. Passing volume should rise somewhat from the current 26 attempts a game. The result is a top-12-ish efficiency passer rather than a top-five one, which is still the best version of him on record.

strengths.title: Accuracy jump without shortening throws
strengths.body: His CPOE ranks first while his intended air yards match his career norm, so this isn't checkdown inflation. The bad-throw rate fell to roughly half his career level, which is the most durable signal in the profile. Some regression is certain off a +10 mark, but the underlying ball placement looks genuinely improved.

strengths.title: Intermediate and middle-of-field throws
strengths.body: Coen's offense is built around 10-19 yard throws, and Lawrence is converting them at a 68.6% success rate. The middle of the field has been his most productive area by a wide margin. Both of his interceptions also came at this depth, so the aggression carries some risk, but it's the right kind.

strengths.title: Ball security this season
strengths.body: He's at a 1.9% interception rate with zero fumbles lost, a sharp break from years of ranking near the bottom in picks. That fits the cleaner ball placement. The fumble side will drift, but the interception rate has a real cause behind it.

concerns.title: Sacks outpacing the pressure he faces
concerns.body: He's pressured on only 16.7% of dropbacks, yet he ranks 26th in sack rate because over a fifth of pressures end in sacks. The line also allows hits at the fourth-worst rate in the league. Cincinnati got him four times in Week 4. This is part protection and part his reluctance to scramble out, and it's the main drain on his efficiency.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate running hot
concerns.body: A 7.7% TD rate and six red-zone scores on 17 attempts are well beyond his career norms. His red-zone completion rate is only 52.9%, so the scoring is outrunning the down-to-down work. Expect touchdown production to fall toward roughly 1.5 a game.

concerns.title: The rushing floor has disappeared
concerns.body: After 290-360 rush yards in four of five seasons, he has 34 through four games with just two scrambles. That costs him a fantasy floor and a way to escape pressure, and it likely feeds the sack rate. It reads as a role or health-free choice rather than decline, since his designed runs have been efficient, but it may simply not come back.

trend.note: Passing yards have stayed in a tight 182-245 band. The only real dud was the Week 2 loss in Denver (-4.1 EPA, 14.3% bad throws while blitzed seven times), and he's posted positive EPA in the other three games.

nextGame.headline: Pressure-starved, banged-up Eagles defense sets up a clean-pocket afternoon
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia's pass defense ranks 22nd in EPA and generates almost nothing up front: last in hit rate and 30th in sack rate. That attacks his biggest weakness, the sacks, directly. Their strength is downfield, sixth in deep EPA allowed and 10th in explosive pass rate. They are much softer underneath and in the middle, which is where Lawrence lives at 10-19 yards.

Availability tilts further toward Jacksonville. LB Zack Baun (97% of snaps) and S Marcus Epps are out, which thins the middle-of-field coverage Lawrence has been carving up, and CB Quinyon Mitchell is questionable with a knee issue. Philadelphia's 29th-ranked offense is missing RT Lane Johnson, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, with C Cam Jurgens in concussion protocol and Saquon Barkley week-to-week. Jacksonville's top-seven defense should control the script, and the Jaguars report no offensive injuries.

keyMatchups.title: Clean pocket against a dead pass rush
keyMatchups.body: The Eagles rank last in hit rate and 30th in sack rate. Lawrence has averaged two sacks a game behind a line that allows hits at a bottom-four rate. This is the week his pressure-to-sack problem should go quiet.

keyMatchups.title: Middle of the field without Baun
keyMatchups.body: His best area by EPA is the middle, and Philadelphia loses its every-down linebacker plus a rotational safety. Expect Washington and Strange to work the seams and in-breakers on intermediate routes.

keyMatchups.title: Game script could cap volume
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th and is missing Johnson, Smith and Goedert, so a Jacksonville lead is likely. He's been sharp when up 9+ (+0.53 EPA), but his two blowout wins came on 23 and 29 attempts. Don't expect a 300-yard day.

nextGame.watch: Whether Philadelphia's lack of pressure finally gives him a game with zero or one sack, and whether he takes the deep shots their secondary defends well or stays patient underneath.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts that should last are the improved ball placement, the intermediate-heavy design and the shotgun-first structure. A defense that ranks seventh in EPA should keep game scripts manageable, too. The parts that won't last are the 7.7% TD rate, the +0.94 deep EPA on 10 throws and probably a CPOE in double digits. Settle him near +3 to +5. With only about 26 attempts a game in a run-balanced offense, his yardage will stay middling even as efficiency holds.

The swing piece is the legs. If the scrambling returns toward his usual 20 yards a game, his fantasy floor rises and some sacks turn into gains. If it doesn't, he's a pure efficiency passer whose weekly output depends on touchdown luck. Interceptions should run higher than the current pace given his history, though below his career-worst years.
swingFactors: Pass protection: offensive hit rate is 29th
How fast the TD rate regresses

bets.reason: Jacksonville is 3-1 against the spread, with a top-seven defense facing a 29th-ranked offense now missing Lane Johnson, DeVonta Smith and Goedert, with Jurgens and Barkley uncertain. A full touchdown is a lot, but the injury gap is wide.

Three of Jacksonville's four games went under, and Philadelphia's offense is 30th in success rate and passes 5.7 points below expectation. A comfortable lead should also slow Jacksonville's pace in the second half.
Philadelphia ranks 30th in sack rate and last in hit rate. That directly offsets the protection issues behind his 7.1% sack rate.

His 7.7% TD rate and six red-zone scores on 17 attempts are well above his career norms, and the game script points to fewer attempts. The 'he's thrown two a game' read overstates his scoring baseline.

confidence.note: Four games and 114 dropbacks; CPOE and TD rate far outside his career range, though the bad-throw drop gives the improvement a real cause.
